nodes.name: Hydrothermal NiFe Hydroxide Synthesis
nodes.procedure: NiFe hydroxide nanosheet arrays were synthesized on pre-cleaned nickel foam (NF) via a hydrothermal method (Figure S1, Supporting Information).
nodes.source_text: NiFe hydroxide nanosheet arrays were synthesized on pre-cleaned nickel foam (NF) via a hydrothermal method (Figure S1, Supporting Information).

nodes.name: Ammonia Calcination to Ni3FeN
nodes.procedure: These arrays were subsequently calcined in a tube furnace under an ammonia atmosphere to form Ni₃FeN/NF.
nodes.source_text: These arrays were subsequently calcined in a tube furnace under an ammonia atmosphere to form Ni₃FeN/NF.

unit_operations.name: Calcination
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: calcined in a tube furnace under an ammonia atmosphere

nodes.name: Rapid Low-Temperature Phosphatization
nodes.procedure: Subsequent surface modification was achieved through rapid low-temperature phosphatization, yielding PO₄³⁻ modified Ni₃FeN/NF (denoted as Ni₃FeN@PO₄³⁻/NF).
nodes.source_text: Subsequent surface modification was achieved through rapid low-temperature phosphatization, yielding PO₄³⁻ modified Ni₃FeN/NF (denoted as Ni₃FeN@PO₄³⁻/NF).

nodes.description: OER LSV performance in 1 M KOH electrolyte
nodes.source_text: Ni₃FeN@PO₄³⁻/NF achieves a current density of 10 mA cm⁻² with an overpotential of just 228 mV... at 100, 500, and 1000 mA cm⁻², Ni₃FeN@PO₄³⁻/NF requires overpotentials of only 258, 295, and 319 mV... Ni₃FeN@PO₄³⁻/NF exhibits a C_dl value of 21.9 mF cm⁻², representing a 34.4% increase compared to Ni₃FeN/NF

nodes.description: OER durability in 1 M KOH electrolyte
nodes.source_text: chronopotentiometry was employed to evaluate the long-term durability of the catalysts during the OER at various current densities. Both catalysts maintained stable operation at ampere-level current densities for at least 200 h, with Ni₃FeN@PO₄³⁻/NF showing no performance degradation even under 2 A cm⁻²

nodes.description: OER LSV performance in alkaline seawater electrolyte at 500 mA/cm²
nodes.source_text: At a current density of 500 mA cm⁻², the η of Ni₃FeN/NF increases significantly from 351 to 428 mV... In contrast, under the same conditions, Ni₃FeN@PO₄³⁻/NF exhibits a comparatively minor η increase, with a mere 34 mV rise

nodes.description: OER durability in alkaline seawater at 1 A/cm²
nodes.source_text: Ni₃FeN@PO₄³⁻/NF displays remarkable durability, operating continuously for up to 2500 h at 1 A cm⁻²

nodes.description: AEMWE overall water splitting in 1 M KOH + seawater
nodes.source_text: In 1 M KOH + seawater electrolyte, the electrolyzer reaches current densities of 0.5 and 1.0 A cm⁻² at applied voltages of only 1.95 and 2.18 V, respectively... The assembled AEMWE demonstrated near-perfect Faraday efficiency and high hydrogen production efficiency... The hydrogen purity reached an outstanding 99.9%

nodes.description: CV activation tests in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: cyclic voltammetry (CV) tests were performed at room temperature using a standard three-electrode system at a scan rate of 50 mV s⁻¹ for 250 cycles (without iR correction)... after 250 continuous CV cycles, the cathodic peak potential of Ni₃FeN@PO₄³⁻/NF shifts by 95 mV, whereas under the same conditions, the cathodic peak potential of Ni₃FeN/NF only shifts by 65 mV

nodes.description: CV activation tests in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: cyclic voltammetry (CV) tests were performed at room temperature using a standard three-electrode system at a scan rate of 50 mV s⁻¹ for 250 cycles (without iR correction)... after 250 continuous CV cycles, the cathodic peak potential of Ni₃FeN@PO₄³⁻/NF shifts by 95 mV

nodes.description: LSV OER in 1 M KOH with Tafel analysis
nodes.source_text: The superior reaction kinetics of Ni₃FeN@PO₄³⁻/NF is further evidenced by its notably lower Tafel slope relative to Ni₃FeN/NF and RuO₂ (Figure 3c). Additionally, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) reveals that Ni₃FeN@PO₄³⁻/NF has the lowest charge transfer resistance

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni₃FeN/NF adopts a simple cubic antiperovskite crystal structure with Pm3m space group.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Rietveld refinement of X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns indicates that the Ni₃FeN/NF adopts a simple cubic antiperovskite crystal structure with a Pm3m space group...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni₃FeN/NF retains nanosheet structure transforming into porous architecture; phosphatization does not change the microstructure of Ni₃FeN/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images reveal that the Ni₃FeN/NF retained its original nanosheet structure while transforming into a porous architecture... SEM images show that the phosphatization process does not change the microstructure of Ni₃FeN/NF.

properties.description: Porous nanofibrous structure with interconnected fibers

nodes.characterization_summary: Interconnected porous nanosheet arrays of Ni₃FeN/NF facilitate rapid charge transport.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images further corroborate this structural evolution, showing that the interconnected porous nanosheet arrays facilitate rapid charge transport...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni₃FeN@PO₄³⁻/NF surface covered by amorphous phosphate layer ≈5 nm thick; internal lattice fringes with spacing of 0.217 nm correspond to (111) planes of Ni₃FeN.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In contrast to the well-defined crystalline edges of the Ni₃FeN/NF, the surface of Ni₃FeN@PO₄³⁻/NF is covered by an amorphous phosphate layer ≈5 nm thick... High-resolution TEM (HRTEM) images show that the internal lattice fringes with a spacing of 0.217 nm, correspond to the (111) planes of the Ni₃FeN.

nodes.characterization_summary: Uniform distribution of Ni, Fe, N, P, and O across Ni₃FeN@PO₄³⁻/NF skeleton with no agglomeration.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) mapping spectra show a uniform distribution of Ni, Fe, N, P, and O across the skeleton, with no agglomeration detected...

nodes.characterization_summary: Both catalysts display characteristic peaks at 550 and 680 cm⁻¹ corresponding to Ni-N and Ni-Fe-N bonds; no significant carbon peaks observed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure S5a (Supporting Information), the Raman spectra of both catalysts display two distinct characteristic peaks centered at 550 and 680 cm⁻¹, corresponding to Ni-N and Ni-Fe-N bonds, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p shows Ni²⁺ at 855.2/872.8 eV and Ni⁺ at 852.5/869.6 eV; Fe 2p shows decreased surface Fe⁺ from 13.19% to 6.2% after phosphating; P 2p shows P-O at 132.9 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Figure 2a, the high-resolution XPS spectrum of Ni 2p reveals two pairs of characteristic peaks. The peaks at 855.2 and 872.8 eV are attributed to Ni²⁺... The high-resolution P 2p XPS spectrum (Figure 2c) shows a prominent peak at 132.9 eV, corresponding to P-O bonds...

nodes.characterization_summary: Both catalysts resemble Ni foil at Ni K-edge and show metallic Ni character; Ni in Ni₃FeN@PO₄³⁻/NF exhibits higher oxidation state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) analysis at the Ni K-edge reveals that both Ni₃FeN/NF and Ni₃FeN@PO₄³⁻/NF closely resemble the Ni foil... indicating the predominance of metallic Ni.

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS shows metal-metal and metal-nitrogen coordination shells; PO₄³⁻ introduction slightly decreases second metal-metal coordination shell intensity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fourier-transformed extended X-ray absorption fine structure (FT-EXAFS) spectra display two distinct peaks... Notably, after the introduction of PO₄³⁻, the intensity of the second metal-metal coordination shell peak for both Ni and Fe slightly decreases...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni₃FeN@PO₄³⁻/NF shows larger Ni²⁺/Ni³⁺ redox peak area, more negative oxidation onset, and 95 mV cathodic peak shift after 250 cycles vs 65 mV for Ni₃FeN/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared to Ni₃FeN/NF, Ni₃FeN@PO₄³⁻/NF exhibits a larger redox peak area and a more negative oxidation onset potential... after 250 continuous CV cycles, the cathodic peak potential of Ni₃FeN@PO₄³⁻/NF shifts by 95 mV, whereas... Ni₃FeN/NF only shifts by 65 mV.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni₃FeN@PO₄³⁻/NF exhibits Cdl value of 21.9 mF cm⁻², 34.4% increase compared to Ni₃FeN/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure S11c (Supporting Information), Ni₃FeN@PO₄³⁻/NF exhibits a Cdl value of 21.9 mF cm⁻², representing a 34.4% increase compared to Ni₃FeN/NF...

nodes.characterization_summary: Both catalysts show surface reconstruction to NiOOH with peaks at ≈475 and 550 cm⁻¹ during OER; Ni₃FeN@PO₄³⁻/NF begins at lower potential (1.40 V vs RHE) with stronger γ-NiOOH signal and stable PO₄³⁻ groups vs Ni₃FeN/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Both catalysts... exhibited noticeable surface reconstruction during the OER process. Distinct peaks at ≈475 and 550 cm⁻¹ were observed... surface reconstruction of Ni₃FeN@PO₄³⁻/NF begins at 1.40 V versus RHE... Ni₃FeN/NF requires... 1.42 V... It is noted that the PO₄³⁻ groups... remain stable during the reactive reconfiguration...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni₃FeN@PO₄³⁻/NF shows lowest charge transfer resistance compared to Ni₃FeN/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Additionally, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) reveals that Ni₃FeN@PO₄³⁻/NF has the lowest charge transfer resistance (Figure S10, Supporting Information)...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni₃FeN@PO₄³⁻/NF phase angle transition begins at 1.42 V vs RHE with faster frequency decline than Ni₃FeN/NF at 1.47 V.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In situ EIS measurements... Ni₃FeN@PO₄³⁻/NF undergoes this transition at just 1.42 V versus RHE with a much faster frequency decline... Ni₃FeN/NF starts to decrease only at 1.47 V...
